packet-13 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. I followed the brief and PROMPT.md only.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Single leaf, upright, photographed on black with ruler at top and colour checker bottom right. Pencil shelfmark on lower strip: "Stams, StA, Frg. 206-1r" (modern).
- Leaf heavily stained, darkened and damaged: holes along left side, right edge of column b torn away irregularly from mid-height down (line ends lost), lower third of page blank/stained below the text. Top and bottom strips are folded-over margins (binding reuse).
- Two columns of text, Gothic textualis, brown-black ink. Roughly 35-37 lines visible per column; text block ends about two-thirds down; the area below appears blank (end of text block or lost).
- Column a: upper part (about lines 1-9) very faded; a gap/very faint zone around lines 10-13 (red marks visible there). Near the foot of col. a an enlarged red initial (looks like "E"/"F") two lines high, with red rubric on the same line: something like "[...]stla vi. Ad Romanos" (tentative, to be checked on tiles).
- Column b: a long red initial (I/J-shaped, descending about 13 lines) at about line 12; a second red initial about line 30 near the foot. Red rubric words at line ~12 right end and line ~31.
- Red touches/paraphs inside text in both columns. No running title visible (top margin is a folded strip). No marginal or interlinear glosses noticed at overview scale.
- Tentative interpretation: liturgical/lectionary-type text with rubricated section headings (rubric naming a reading). This is an interpretation only.

Ink here is very faded and abraded; most words are only partly legible. Readings are low-confidence.
